mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-86.3 to -81.1), indicating an established recovery trend; this momentum is expected to persist, pushing average RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks higher than the prior 4-week average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically from -86.3 to -81.1 over last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior 4-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 points within a single week (as it did from t-2w to t-1w, -78.3 to -76.1), commuters and shoppers resume transit-dependent retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -78.3 to -76.1 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 2 weeks after a TRANSIT week-on-week gain exceeding 5 points in more than half of observed cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES (-69.6 to -65.3) and TRANSIT (-79.4 to -75.1) over the last 3 weeks jointly signals restored daily routines; their combined upward movement amplifies retail footfall more than either series alone, raising RETAIL_REC over 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over 4 weeks even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show concurrent multi-week improvement, falsifying the interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS mobility exceeding 10 points (as seen from t-2w -62.1 to t-1w -51.3) indicates relaxation of outdoor gathering restrictions, a signal that typically precedes loosening of retail restrictions and higher RETAIL_REC within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -62.1 to -51.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 2 weeks following a PARKS week-on-week increase exceeding 10 points in a majority of comparable cases.

mechanism_narrative: The plateau in PARKS mobility at -51.3 for two consecutive weeks (t-1w, t-0w) suggests seasonal outdoor activity has stabilized after an initial spring surge, implying retail recovery will also plateau rather than continue rising, keeping RETAIL_REC roughly flat to slightly lower over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS held flat at -51.3 for t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 4 weeks despite PARKS showing no further week-on-week improvement.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 25.0 (crossing threshold, as occurred at t-0w with 24.7), it signals reduced stay-at-home behavior, freeing time for discretionary retail trips and raising RETAIL_REC within 1 week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped to 24.7 at t-0w, crossing below 25.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following RESIDENTIAL crossing below 25.0 in the majority of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility converging toward baseline (-48.1 to -39.0 over 4 weeks) reflects easing of essential-only shopping restrictions; as this convergence continues, broader retail restrictions are expected to ease in parallel, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -48.1 to -39.0 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even as GROCERY_PHARM continues its convergence toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, concurrent TRANSIT improvement and RESIDENTIAL decline jointly indicate commuters are both leaving home more and using transit more, a combined signal that drives retail footfall up faster than either series predicts alone, raising RETAIL_REC within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose and RESIDENTIAL fell concurrently each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks despite simultaneous TRANSIT gains and RESIDENTIAL declines, indicating no interaction effect.
